findings.summary: Milestone M1.D2 enumerates required schema deliverables for the subsystem contracts yet omits the explicit definition of the 'plan_package_final.json' input schema, which is required by R1 and Capsule Goal 2.

evidence.note: R1 requires the subsystem to accept a structured plan_package_final.json input.
evidence.quote: accept exactly one frozen plan_package_final.json (plus its associated structured handoff bundle)

evidence.note: M1.D2 lists specific contract schemas (repo_context, workspace_context, etc.) but fails to list the plan_package_final schema definition.
evidence.quote: Typed/versioned JSON schemas and contracts: repo_context.json, workspace_context.json, stage_handoff.json...

evidence.note: Capsule Goal 2 explicitly requires definition of the canonical input contract.
evidence.quote: Define the canonical input contract: accept plan_package_final.json only...

findings.summary: Milestone M1 defines 'specification' deliverables (workflow specs, schemas, governance rules) but lacks execution milestones for implementing the subsystem described in functional requirements R1-R3, creating a traceability gap between functional requirements and plan realization.

evidence.note: R1 describes a runtime functional behavior of the target subsystem.
evidence.quote: The Implementation Council subsystem SHALL accept exactly one frozen plan_package_final.json...

evidence.note: M1 deliverables are specifications for the design, not the implementation of the system functions.
evidence.quote: Deterministic linear workflow specification (state machine)...

evidence.note: Exit criteria confirms the milestone standard is specification-complete, not implementation-complete.
evidence.quote: Architecture option O1 is fully specified... preserving separation of powers...

findings.summary: Sample check for R1 is not fully covered by AT1: it tests runs where the chat log/non-canonical artifact is the only planning input, but does not test the stricter requirement that plan_package_final.json must be the sole canonical planning input when additional non-canonical inputs are also provided (risk: mixed-input runs could still be accepted and non-canonical content could influence semantics).

evidence.note: R1 requires plan_package_final.json as sole canonical planning input
evidence.quote: SHALL accept exactly one frozen plan_package_final.json... as its sole canonical planning input, and SHALL reject chat logs or any non-canonical/unapproved upstream artifacts...

evidence.note: AT1 only tests chat/non-canonical as the only planning input
evidence.quote: Attempt to initiate... with inputs: (a) valid plan_package_final.json... (b) a chat log reference as the only planning input; (c) an unapproved non-canonical artifact as planning input.

findings.summary: Sample checks for R2 and R3 rely on “schema-invalid”/“schema-valid” repo_context.json and workspace_context.json, but the candidate package does not provide an explicit, traceable reference to the actual typed/versioned schema artifacts or their version identifiers within the sample-checked trace (risk: acceptance tests can’t be implemented deterministically without a concrete schema reference).

evidence.note: R2 requires typed/versioned repo_context.json schema enforcement
evidence.quote: SHALL define and require a typed, versioned repo_context.json schema; orchestrator validators SHALL fail the run if repo_context.json is missing or schema-invalid...

evidence.note: AT2 invokes schema validity but does not cite a concrete schema artifact
evidence.quote: Start a run without repo_context.json; then... with repo_context.json that violates schema; then... with schema-valid repo_context.json...

evidence.note: R3 requires typed/versioned workspace_context.json schema enforcement
evidence.quote: SHALL define and require a typed, versioned workspace_context.json schema; orchestrator validators SHALL fail the run if workspace_context.json is missing or schema-invalid...

evidence.note: AT3 invokes schema validity but does not cite a concrete schema artifact
evidence.quote: Start a run without workspace_context.json; then... with schema-invalid workspace_context.json; then... with schema-valid workspace_context.json...

evidence.note: Milestone expects typed/versioned JSON schemas but sample-checked trace does not point to concrete schema artifacts/versions
evidence.quote: Typed/versioned JSON schemas and contracts: repo_context.json, workspace_context.json, stage_handoff.json, ChangeRequest schema...

findings.summary: R1 requirement text does not explicitly mandate rejection of chat logs in the requirement statement itself; the rejection behavior is implied by 'sole canonical planning input' but not stated as a SHALL reject clause.

evidence.note: R1 text states 'SHALL accept exactly one frozen plan_package_final.json' and 'SHALL reject chat logs' but the SHALL reject is embedded in a compound sentence rather than a separate SHALL clause.
evidence.quote: SHALL accept exactly one frozen plan_package_final.json... and SHALL reject chat logs or any non-canonical/unapproved upstream artifacts

findings.summary: AT1 acceptance test references 'structured errors' for rejection but does not specify whether these errors must conform to a typed schema or can be freeform text, creating potential ambiguity in validator implementation.

evidence.note: Pass criteria mentions 'structured errors' without defining structure requirements.
evidence.quote: runs (b) and (c) are rejected with structured errors indicating non-canonical planning inputs are not authoritative

findings.summary: R2 and R3 both use 'SHALL be required before any code-generation stage begins' and 'SHALL be required before any workspace-writing stage begins' respectively, but the architecture does not explicitly define which stages are 'code-generation' vs 'workspace-writing' stages, creating potential enforcement ambiguity.

evidence.note: R2 requires repo_context.json before 'any code-generation stage' but does not define which stages qualify.
evidence.quote: SHALL be required before any code-generation stage begins

evidence.note: R3 requires workspace_context.json before 'any workspace-writing stage' but does not define which stages qualify.
evidence.quote: SHALL be required before any workspace-writing stage begins

evidence.note: Dataflow describes stages but does not explicitly tag which are code-generation vs workspace-writing.
evidence.quote: 1) Intake Gate validates... 2) Work Plan Compiler... 3) Generate: Writer Pod produces diff-only patchset artifacts

findings.summary: AT2 and AT3 acceptance tests specify 'schema-valid repo_context.json' and 'schema-valid workspace_context.json' but the schemas themselves are listed as deliverables (M1.D2) rather than being present in the current artifact set, making the tests unverifiable until schemas are delivered.

evidence.note: AT2 requires schema-valid repo_context.json but schema is not yet present.
evidence.quote: run with schema-valid repo_context.json containing required fields... is accepted

evidence.note: AT3 requires schema-valid workspace_context.json but schema is not yet present.
evidence.quote: run with schema-valid workspace_context.json containing required fields... is accepted

evidence.note: Schemas are listed as future deliverables, not current artifacts.
evidence.quote: Typed/versioned JSON schemas and contracts: repo_context.json, workspace_context.json...
